correctness.rationale: For a rank-one tensor u⊗φ, the commutation of T with nilpotent N forces Nu=0 and φN=0; T²=0 iff φ(u)=0. Restricted K×Ann(im N) pairing has rank a (#singleton blocks) and radical dimension s=b+c. Counting its projective incidence tensors gives total C, upward C_+ = (q^a−1)q^s(q^(r−1)−q^s)/(q−1), downward C_- = (q^b−1)q^c q^(s−1)/(q−1) for b>0, and C_0=C−C_+−C_-. Downward update is detected by the predecessor map on E=kerN∩imN of rank b. Since NT=TN=T²=0, higher powers of N+T equal N^j (j≥2), so only the 1↔2 Jordan-block transition occurs. The square-zero rank-one incidence is a cone over a bilinear divisor of coefficient rank a; it has two geometric components iff a=1 (otherwise irreducible). For a=1, n≥2 implies r≥2, avoiding the degenerate component intersection boundary. Independent GF(2) direct matrices checked partitions (2,1,1),(3,2),(2,2),(4,1),(3,1,1),(1,1,1), with all delta multiplicities matching.
